title: AI warned Real Sociedad against appointing trophy-winning American coach
content:
The president of Spanish soccer club Real Sociedad has revealed that artificial intelligence (AI) told him not to appoint Pellegrino Matarazzo as head coach earlier in the season.

On Saturday, 48-year-old Matarazzo guided the Basque club to the Copa del Rey title with a penalty shootout victory over Atletico Madrid, less than four months after his appointment. In doing so, he became the first U.S.-born manager to win a trophy at a club in a top-five European league.

Real Sociedad president Jokin Aperribay told Spanish radio station Cadena Ser on Monday that the club’s sporting director Erik Bretos drove the appointment, and his own initial scepticism of the move was not helped by asking AI.

“Erik told me Matarazzo, and I asked the AI ​​if he was a good coach for Real Sociedad; it said no,” Aperribay explained. “Thank goodness I trusted Erik!”

Matarazzo, raised in Fair Lawn, New Jersey and the son of Italian immigrants, previously coached Bundesliga clubs Stuttgart and Hoffenheim but prior to joining Real Sociedad, he had no previous experience in Spanish football.

“I didn’t know him, and in our first meeting, I was impressed because he knew everything about everyone,” Aperribay said of the appointment. “He had an amazing analysis of Real Sociedad.”

Aperribay added that, after Real Sociedad eliminated Basque rivals Athletic Club from the Copa semi-final stage, he asked AI again if Matarazzo was a good fit for the club. “It told me he was an excellent appointment!”

When Matarazzo was appointed, Real Sociedad had collected just 17 points from their opening 17 league games and were struggling in the lower half of La Liga.

The team has won 25 points in the 14 games since, and are now seventh in the standings with seven games remaining — four points from Real Betis in fifth, and potential Champions League qualification for next season.
